chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Write for them if you know in them any good.' He said: 'If you know for them religion and wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'good' mean in the Quranic verse about freeing slaves?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a specific exegetical clarification for the term 'good' (khayran) in Surah An-Nur, restricting it to the slave's adherence to Islam and financial solvency. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on both spiritual integrity and economic capability as prerequisites for the validity of the mukatabah contract, ensuring the master's confidence in the slave's ability to fulfill the agreement.
